samples.summary: Visual verification lane now hard-depends on a third-party CDN (fonts.googleapis.com) for pass/fail
samples.evidence: The change adds `Inter`, `Fraunces`, `JetBrains Mono` (the families index.html:12 fetches from https://fonts.googleapis.com) to VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES and gates capture on `document.fonts.check()` for each (lines 384-393, 10s timeout) plus a poll that no FontFace remains `status: "loading"` (394-398). The rendered bytes that become the accepted baseline are therefore whatever a third party serves at run time: an attacker able to influence DNS/TLS/proxying for fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com on the CI runner controls glyph rendering and can either fail the lane at will (DoS on the pipeline) or, in a `UPDATE_VISUAL_BROWSER_BASELINE=true` run (line 15/533), poison committed baselines with attacker-influenced pixels. There is no integrity pin (css2 responses cannot carry SRI, and index.html:10-13 has none) and no local/self-hosted font fallback. Impact is limited to build integrity/availability, not the shipped app, hence minor; the exposure is real and enlarged by this diff.

samples.summary: `weights` is interpolated into the Google Fonts css2 URL without encoding (family is encoded, weights is not)
samples.evidence: `familyParam()` does `family=${encodeURIComponent(family)}:wght@${weights ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS}` — the family is escaped but `weights` is concatenated raw and the result is assigned to a `<link rel=stylesheet>` href (font-catalog.ts:161-162). A `weights` value containing `&` or `?` would inject extra query segments into the stylesheet request (e.g. `400&family=Something`), i.e. attacker-chosen additional font families/params requested on behalf of the user. I traced every call site (`more-fonts-dialog.tsx:135`, `apply-font-family.ts:28`, `pdf-actions.ts:31`, `theme-builder-panel.tsx:100`, `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:349`) and all of them pass only `family`, so `weights` currently comes from the static FONT_CATALOG — I could not complete an exploit chain, hence low confidence. It is out of the diff and pre-existing; raised because the diff's whole subject is this font-loading path. Encoding `weights` (or validating it against `^[0-9;]+$`) closes it.
